designSummary: Randomised comparison with duty days as clusters; alerts analysed individually with day as a random effect.
sampleSize: About 890 alerts over six months, about 445 per arm, with about five alerts a day. Time to decision is right-skewed; on the log scale with a standard deviation near 0.9 and an intracluster correlation near 0.1 (design effect about 1.4, claim c3), the effective sample is about 318 alerts per arm, giving 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a ratio of median times of about 0.82, an 18 percent reduction. About 4 percent of alerts are real (claim c4), so each arm will see about 18 true events, too few for a statistical comparison of missed events.
primaryAnalysis: Linear mixed model of log time to decision with procedure, syndrome and weekday as fixed effects and duty day as a random intercept; the result is reported as a ratio of geometric mean times with its 95 percent confidence interval.
secondaryAnalysis: Escalations per 100 alerts by procedure with a mixed logistic model; dismissed true events listed and reviewed individually; contamination reported monthly.
missingData: Alerts without a recorded decision time are counted and reported; the primary analysis excludes them, with a sensitivity analysis assigning them the 95th percentile time of their arm.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes reported with confidence intervals only.
software: R with lme4; allocation list and analysis code held by the analyst outside the rota.
overfittingGuards: Two adjustment variables fixed in advance
Safety review criteria fixed before the first study day
summary: About 445 alerts per arm; 80 percent power for an 18 percent shorter decision time; missed events reviewed case by case.
